body.p: There was once a man by the name Alig̣yáx̂ who had a wife and two small boys. He started killing the relatives of his wife and then proceeded to kill other inhabitants of his village. He went to another village in order to look for another wife. He found a woman and married her. Then he came back to the village where he had lived before and killed all the rest of the people. He left only his first wife and her two boys. Then he took all his belongings, boat, tools and weapons and moved to the village of his new wife. To his former wife and children he left absolutely nothing.
When he joined his new wife he tried to provide her with everything she needed or was short of. And so they lived together.

His former wife left with her two boys without any food, gathered seaweed for their food. The boys who were often out of doors, had a chance
to see many small birds. As they did not know what to call them, they asked their mother the birds' name. She said:
"Your kinsmen - your mother's brothers, your grandfathers, your great-grandfathers – called these small birds sparrows; they used to snare them, kill them and eat them."
"Mother," said one of the boys, "if we had snares, we too could catch and use them as food."

Thereupon the mother glanced up and saw some snares hanging from the ceiling of the dugout. She took them down and gave them to the boys. They left with the snares and after spending a whole day in catching sparrows they brought a great number of them to their mother. She hastened to skin them and cooked the meat. Thus the boys continued to catch sparrows and for a long time all the three lived on their meat. The mother also dressed the birds' skins and made coats of them for her sons.

One day the boys went to the shore looking for animals cast up by the sea and found a thong-seal. They brought it to their mother. She skinned it and they ate the meat. The boys again went to the shore to look for animals and found a stranded sea-lion. They took it home and the mother skinned it and they fed on the meat. The mother dried the skins of the seal and sea-lion and stored them.

On another occasion the boys after having passed a day in the open home and said to their mother: "Mother, if we had a kayak we could go out to sea and catch sea mammals. Not having a kayak we must be satisfied with creatures cast up by the sea."

So the mother went out to the spot where the people used to build kayaks. As she walked along she picked up parts of a kayak's frame and made a kayak for her boys. When the kayak was finished, the family went to a deserted house to have a feast. The boys asked about their father. The mother told them that he had killed all their relatives and abandoned his children. Then the boys decided to kill their father and they started to train themselves for it. When evening came they sang and instead of drumming clapped their hands until flames sprang from their palms. The mother made many darts for them to hurl.
On the following day they went out hunting and killed many thong-seals and asked the mother to store their skins.

They asked again where they might find their father. She named the place to which he had gone, but said that she did not know if he was still alive. She was afraid to let her boys go. But they insisted and she permitted them to go, begging them to return soon.

The boys started off in their kayak and soon reached the place where their father lived. They were received as guests and given food. Two men put a big plate of edibles before them. When they had eaten, the older son poured out the rest of the food. Their father, who had not recognized them, prepared a feast for them. The people of the house danced, and when they had finished the boys prepared to dance. They were given a drum but they refused to take it. While they were dancing they sang:

lg.l: "Both sons of Alig̣yáx̂ are still alive."

body.p: When their father heard this he recognized them. While singing and dancing the boys tried to come close to the entrance ladder. Then they looked at each other and began to clap their hands. Flames sprang from their palms and set everything in the dwelling on fire. The boys made haste to leave the dugout. Standing on the roof they forced everyone who appeared on the ladder in the entrance hole back into the dugout. When their father appeared they said to him:
"You had abandoned us so that we might die, now you shall die."
And they hurled him down into the burning dugout.
After killing all the inhabitants of the father's village they returned to their mother and began to live well, it is said.
